m:marais: All free. A little-known passage: the garden of the Hôtel de Sully, on Rue Saint-Antoine, leads straight under the arcades of the square.
m:notredame: The towers are visited separately: €16, 424 steps, online booking only.
m:louvre: The museum is closed on Tuesdays and a visit would need half a day: on a day trip it's best enjoyed from outside.
m:eiffel: Going up costs from €14.80 (on foot to the 2nd floor) to €36.70 (lift to the top); from 29 September 2026 stair tickets must also be booked online. After sunset, at the start of every hour, the tower sparkles for a few minutes.
m:arc: Going up to the terrace is paid; looking at it from outside is free.
m:montmartre: The basilica is free. In front of the steps watch out for people offering bracelets «as a gift» and for pickpockets.
m:louvremus: Ticket €22 for EU residents (€32 for others), free under 18 and for EU residents under 26. Closed on Tuesdays; Wednesday and Friday open until 9pm. Book your time slot on ticket.louvre.fr: without a booking you only get in if places are left.
m:orsay: Ticket €16 online, free for EU residents under 26. Closed on Mondays; Thursdays open until 9:45pm.
m:stgermain: All free. The historic cafés on the square are expensive: for a coffee, move one street over.
m:latin: The garden is free and closes at sunset (the time changes with the seasons). Inside the Panthéon: €11.50, open every day.
m:opera: Self-guided visit €15 for EU residents (€25 for others), online only on operadeparis.fr: no tickets are sold at the desk. Open 10am–5pm (last entry half an hour before). The auditorium may be closed for rehearsals. The Galeries Lafayette rooftop is free and may close in bad weather.
m:canal: All free. On Sunday afternoons the canal banks are pedestrianised.
m:perelachaise: Free entry. Until 5 November open 8am–6pm (Saturday from 8:30am, Sunday from 9am); from 6 November winter hours apply and it closes earlier: check on paris.fr. At the main entrance there's a map of the graves.
m:versailles: Passport ticket (palace, gardens and Trianon) from €22, €32 on Grandes Eaux and Jardins musicaux days (April to October); €3 more for non-EU visitors. The entry time is compulsory. Closed on Mondays; open 9am–6:30pm from April to October, 9am–5:30pm from November to March.
m:trianon: Included in the Passport. The Trianon opens at noon. The park is big: it's about a 30-minute walk from one end to the other.
vd:dheilly: A boulangerie-pâtisserie a short walk from the Châtelet exit: croissants, pain au chocolat and the caramel brioche. Few seats, best for takeaway.
vd:marnay: A neighbourhood bakery between Châtelet and the Centre Pompidou, open on Sundays too: highly praised baguette tradition and croissants. No tables.
vd:tranche: A bakery-café with a few little tables, 3 minutes from Place des Vosges: good if you want to sit down with a cappuccino.
vp:tranche: Coffee and viennoiserie under €10 (menu not seen).
vd:brigat: A pâtisserie 50 metres from Place des Vosges: croissants, flan, tarts and ice cream too. A few little tables inside.
vd:augustins: A tiny bistro on the Seine embankment, opposite the Île de la Cité, famous for its gratins. Few tables and a small kitchen: allow for a bit of a wait.
vd:buci: A Saint-Germain bistro with period furnishings, popular with Parisians too: onion soup, braised beef, crème brûlée.
vd:victoires: A classic, no-frills bistro behind Place des Victoires, among the cheapest in the centre: confit de canard, onion soup, crème brûlée. It fills up early.
vp:victoires: Budget range for Paris (menu not seen).
vd:louise: A small bistro a short walk from the Louvre and the Palais-Royal: escargots, coq au vin, much-praised mash.
vp:louise: Fair prices according to reviews (menu not seen).
vd:richelieu: A neighbourhood bistro behind the Palais-Royal, with the kitchen open all day: onion soup, bourguignon, tartare.
vd:caillou: A small, cosy bistro 10 minutes from the Eiffel Tower, away from the crowds: bourguignon, confit, profiteroles.
vd:crepuscule: A neighbourhood crêperie on a side street near Rue Cler: savoury buckwheat galettes and sweet crêpes, generous portions.
vp:crepuscule: A galette with a cider should stay under €15 (menu not seen).
vd:rozell: A family crêperie below the Sacré-Cœur, praised for galettes and salted caramel crêpes made to order.
vp:rozell: Galette + crêpe + drink €15.90 (2025 price); a galette on its own stays under €15.
vd:crepmm: A small new crêperie near Anvers, with homemade chocolate and cream. Open all day.
vp:crepmm: A galette with a cider should stay under €15 (menu not seen).
vd:phenicien: A neighbourhood Lebanese at the foot of Montmartre: falafel, hummus, tabbouleh. You can also take away.
vp:phenicien: With a sandwich or a falafel plate you stay under €15 (menu not seen); mixed mezze cost more.
vd:broceliande: A Breton crêperie on Rue des Trois Frères, crispy galettes and gluten-free options too. No dinner on Mondays and Tuesdays.
vp:broceliande: Reasonable prices according to reviews (menu not seen).
vd:stlouis: An Île Saint-Louis bakery with sandwiches, quiche and croque-monsieur to take away.
vp:stlouis: Sandwich + drink + dessert deal at €9.50 (from reviews).
vd:berthillon: The historic ice creams and sorbets of the Île Saint-Louis, since 1954. Note: other bars on the island sell its ice cream, but the original shop is at no. 29-31.
vd:castel: A boulangerie a short walk from the Louvre: croissants, pain au chocolat and sandwiches to eat in the Palais-Royal gardens.
vp:castel: Croissants and sandwiches for a few euros.
vd:marques: A neighbourhood boulangerie 10 minutes from the Eiffel Tower, with a queue of Parisians in the morning. Great for a sandwich to eat on the Champ de Mars.
vd:pauline: An artisan pâtisserie on the Rue Cler market street: tarte tatin, éclairs, chocolate tart.
vp:pauline: A pastry for a few euros.
vd:grenier: An award-winning boulangerie for its baguette: try the pain suisse and the madeleines too.
vd:painpain: An artisan Montmartre boulangerie: éclairs, chausson aux pommes and focaccia warmed to order.
vd:manege: A kiosk next to the carousel on Place des Abbesses, 15 metres from the Mur des je t'aime: crêpes on the go, savoury ones too.
vp:manege: Low prices for the area, coffee €1.50 (from reviews).
vd:union: A neighbourhood boulangerie in the 9th arrondissement, famous for its brownie and baguette tradition; the croissants and kouign-amann are great too. No tables.
vd:miche: A neighbourhood bakery-pâtisserie with a very friendly owner: coffee éclairs, almond pain au chocolat and sandwiches on fresh baguette.
vd:quignon: A boulangerie with a few tables: flaky croissants, flan and breakfast sandwiches.
vd:auvergne: A small family-run bakery between the Opéra and Montmartre: almond croissants and chouquettes.
vd:lucette: A cosy crêperie with outdoor seating: galettes and crêpes between €7 and €11, at lunch a two-course deal with a drink at €17.50 (from reviews).
vp:lucette: A galette with a cider stays under €15.
vd:lorette: A brasserie frequented by locals: pepper steak-frites, leeks in vinaigrette, pain perdu.
vd:suzette: A small crêperie on Rue Cadet, a pedestrian shopping street: homemade caramel and chocolate, outdoor tables.
vp:suzette: Low prices according to reviews: galettes and crêpes under €15.
vd:galetezen: Breton galettes with quality ingredients and craft cider; a short menu. Lunch only on Mondays.
vd:fournil: A boulangerie at the bottom of Rue Mouffetard, the Latin Quarter's market street: very light croissants and quiches warmed to order.
vd:gisele: A crêperie-bistro open from 7am to midnight, a short walk from Saint-Germain: generous galettes, at breakfast too.
vp:gisele: A galette stays under €15 (menu not seen).
vd:tournbride: A neighbourhood bistro on Rue Mouffetard: duck confit, sausage with mash, tarte aux pommes. In the morning, coffee and croissants too.
vd:vieuxbistrot: An old-fashioned bistro on Rue Mouffetard: onion soup, bourguignon, crème brûlée. On Tuesdays and Wednesdays it only opens in the evening.
vd:perraudin: A historic bistro a short walk from the Panthéon, with checked tablecloths: steak-frites and bourguignon.
vd:clown: A much-loved crêperie near Saint-Sulpice: a huge menu of buckwheat galettes, homemade chocolate. Lunch only on Mondays.
vp:clown: Affordable prices according to reviews: galette and cider under €15.
vd:germain: A mosaic-decorated crêperie a short walk from Saint-Michel; at lunch a two-crêpe deal from €11 (from reviews).
vd:littlebreizh: A tiny, authentic Breton crêperie: you can watch the crêpes being made in the kitchen. Closed on Sundays and Mondays.
vp:littlebreizh: Fair prices according to reviews (menu not seen).
vd:copains: A neighbourhood boulangerie-café near the Gare de l'Est, with prices for locals: vanilla flan and sandwiches made to order.
vd:marie: A boulangerie a short walk from the Canal Saint-Martin: pistachio and chocolate escargots, sourdough bread.
vd:robinet: A bistro on the Canal Saint-Martin with classic French cooking: duck confit, snails, cheeses. Best to book in the evening.
vd:bistrotpere: A neighbourhood bistro at the Père-Lachaise exit, frequented by locals: roast chicken, salads, tiramisu.
vd:tablespl: A bistro opposite the cemetery: excellent croissants in the morning, generous dishes at lunch.
vd:auguste: A simple place near Père-Lachaise: bagels, burgers, salads and soups; soup and coffee for €7 (from reviews).
vd:cantina: A neighbourhood pizzeria-bar between Père-Lachaise and Oberkampf. The kitchen closes before the bar: ask at the table.
vp:cantina: A pizza is around €15 (menu not seen).
vd:fermepains: A neighbourhood boulangerie a few minutes from the station, with a queue of locals: baguettes, croissants and sandwiches for a picnic in the gardens.
vd:polome: A bakery-pâtisserie near the palace, open every day: croissants, salads and wraps to take away.
vd:blenoir: A crêperie 5 minutes from the palace, generous portions and fair prices for the area.
vp:blenoir: A galette stays under €15 (menu not seen).
vd:tonton: A crêperie popular with Versailles locals, buckwheat galettes; galette, crêpe and drink deal at €18 (from reviews).
vd:carre: A crêperie in Versailles' Saint-Louis district, cider and beer on tap, lunch deals.
cd:orangerie: Monet's great Water Lilies in two oval rooms inside the Tuileries Garden, plus a small Impressionist collection.
cd:rodin: The Thinker and The Kiss in the garden of an 18th-century mansion: open-air sculptures and rooms with plaster casts.
cd:conciergerie: The old prison where Marie Antoinette was held: great Gothic halls on the Île de la Cité.
cd:arcsu: The terrace on top of the arch: twelve avenues radiating like a star and the view of the Eiffel Tower.
cd:catacombes: A kilometre and a half of underground tunnels with the bones of six million Parisians.
cx:catacombes: Entry only with a ticket booked online for a specific time.
cd:quaibranly: Art and cultures of Africa, Asia, Oceania and the Americas in a Jean Nouvel building with a vertical garden.
cd:garnier: The marble staircase, the gilded foyer and the auditorium with Chagall's painted ceiling.
cd:picassop: The largest collection of Picasso's works, in a Marais mansion.
cd:cluny: The museum of the Middle Ages, with the Lady and the Unicorn tapestries and the Roman baths.
cd:flv: The contemporary art museum designed by Frank Gehry, in the Bois de Boulogne, with panoramic terraces.
cd:senna: An hour on the river among the bridges, Notre-Dame, the Louvre and the illuminated Eiffel Tower.
cd:montparnasse: The skyscraper from which you can see all of Paris, Eiffel Tower included.
